subject: Clarify p50/p95 commitments and measurement horizon for hosted API
messages:
From: Amanda Lin <amanda@neohealth.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — p50/p95 and measurement horizon

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked great. We’re starting the procurement review and have two open items from our infra and legal teams:

1) On p50/p95 latency commitments, we need a short write-up that scopes exactly what is measured (client RTT vs. service processing) and whether KV cache hits are included in the latency window.
2) Measurement horizon: our ops team wants to know how charges and SLO compliance are evaluated over time — is it a rolling 30d window, calendar month, or something else? We also need to understand daypart carve-outs for scheduled maintenance or known burst migration windows.

We want to avoid hard-coded p95 penalties while our initial rollout sees big variance during onboarding traffic spikes. Is there a path for a temporary exception during the first 60 days after go-live?

Could you send a short summary (1–2 pages) and any proposed contract language? We’ll share with procurement.

Best,
Amanda
VP Engineering, NeoHealth AI
--
Amanda Lin
NeoHealth AI
amanda@neohealth.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lin <amanda@neohealth.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — p50/p95 and measurement horizon

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short proposal (proposed-slo-amendment-v1.pdf) that we can iterate on. Summary below so procurement can see the key points quickly: 

- What we measure: Redwood’s hosted API latency SLOs (p50/p95) are measured at the Redwood ingress egress boundary — specifically server-side response completion as observed by our edge collectors (service processing + egress to our public API load balancer). Client-side RTT (customer network) is not included in the committed measurement.

- KV cache behavior: p50/p95 measurements include responses served from model execution that may benefit from in-memory KV cache or prefix cache. We tag cached responses in telemetry; if you want cache-exempt measurements we can provide an alternate metric set for evals but the standard SLO includes typical cached behavior.

- Measurement horizon: default is a rolling 30-day window (UTC) for operational alerts and SLA calculations. For contract-level compliance we compute monthly snapshots but allowances (see below) can be defined per contract.

- Daypart carve-outs & scheduled maintenance: scheduled maintenance windows (announced 48h) are excluded from uptime calculations. Short, pre-agreed regional migrations (e.g., database or cluster rebalancing) can be carved out if included in the contract annex.

- Temporary onboarding exception: we can offer a 60-day onboarding exception for p95 enforcement that: (a) excludes the first 14 days from penalties but still reports metrics; (b) applies a graduated remediation plan between days 15–60 with mutually agreed thresholds. This is intended only for first-time go-lives at scale and must be explicitly invoked in the SOW.

Next steps: if this aligns with NeoHealth’s needs, I’ll loop in Ben (account lead) and legal to propose contract language for a short amendment.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed-slo-amendment-v1.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-23T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — p50/p95 and measurement horizon

Adding a few technical clarifications that Nina in Ops (cc’d on our internal thread) asked to have on record — feel free to include in the proposal PDF: 

- Measurement tags: every request we observe gets tagged with model variant, region, cache_hit boolean, and routing tier. Our p50/p95 used for customer-facing commitments aggregates across routing tiers unless the contract specifies tiered commitments.

- Aggregation buckets: the rolling 30-day computation is derived from hourly buckets (UTC). Each hourly bucket computes p50/p95 across requests ingested in that hour; monthly snapshots re-aggregate from those hourly buckets to avoid reprocessing raw traces for compliance audits.

- Burst carve-out mechanics: for a temporary carve-out (like a first-60-day onboarding), we implement a flag that excludes specific request groups (by customer id + onboarding tag) from penalty evaluation while still recording metrics for transparency. This is operationally light but must be requested before the go-live window.

- Example clause language suggestion: 
  "For the first sixty (60) days following activation, Redwood will exclude onboarding-tagged traffic from p95 penalty calculations. During this period, Redwood will provide weekly latency reports and will work with Customer to apply mitigations. After day 60 the standard SLO measurement applies."

Happy to provide a short Ops runbook if NeoHealth wants details on the onboarding tag flow.

—Rishi
Director, Inference Reliability

Kimberly / Rishi — this is helpful, thanks. Two quick follow-ups from procurement and infra after internal review: 

1) Procurement would like the temporary onboarding exception documented and signed — they attached a preliminary PO (purchase-order-NEO-20261124.pdf). We’re okay with the 14-day reporting-only then 15–60 graduated remediation approach, but need defined reporting cadence and an SLA owner.

2) Infra asked whether Redwood can supply a cache-exempt p95 for the first 30 days as a separate telemetry feed — that would help us prove backend performance during our client-side integration tests.

Can you confirm owners and a one-week timeline to get final language into a contract addendum? If so, procurement will route the PO.

Amanda
